title: Artin schreier degree p
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $A\to B\to C$ be injective local maps of complete discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ [def-pc-field-extension], and $M/L$ finite. Write $k_R=R/\mathfrak m_R$ for a residue field. Assume $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ and $\operatorname{char}(k_A)=p$. For any injective local map $R\to S$ of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $E\subseteq Q$ and finite field extension $E'/E$, let $R'$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $E'$ and $S'$ that of $S$ in $(Q\otimes_E E')_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Call $E'/E$ a weak solution if, for every maximal ideal $q$ of $S'$, its contraction $n$ in $R'$ is maximal, $R'_n,S'_q$ are discrete valuation rings, and $nS'_q=qS'_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Reduction is quotient by nilpotents; finite means finite-dimensional; local means pulling back the maximal ideal. Assume $\operatorname{char}(K)=p$, $M/L$ is Galois of degree $p$ (normal and separable), and $k_A=\bigcap_{n\geq0}k_B^{p^n}$ inside $k_B$, where $k_B^{p^n}=\{x^{p^n}:x\in k_B\}$. There is a finite separable extension $K_1/K$, totally ramified with respect to $A$, which is a weak solution for $A\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. A finite separable extension is totally ramified with respect to a complete DVR when its integral closure is a DVR with unchanged residue field and ramification index equal to the field degree; the ramification index $e$ is defined by $\mathfrak m_R S=\mathfrak m_S^e$. A field extension is normal if every irreducible polynomial over the base with a root in the extension splits there.

proof.text: By the Artin–Schreier presentation, choose $z\in M$ with $M=L[z]$, $\xi=z^p-z\in L$, and $M\cong L[T]/(T^p-T-\xi)$. Write $\wp(x)=x^p-x$. For every $h\in L$, replacing $z$ by $z+h$ preserves $L[z]=M$ and replaces $\xi$ by $\xi+\wp(h)$, by direct expansion in characteristic $p$.

Apply the complete-DVR normalization node to $B$ and the finite extension $M/L$. Its uniqueness clause identifies the given local DVR $C$ with the integral closure of $B$ in $M$, and its other clauses give completeness and module finiteness. Subsequently normalizations over $B$ and over $C$ in a field extension of $M$ coincide: the normalization $D'$ over $B$ contains $C$, is integral over $C$ (the same monic equations work), and is integrally closed, so every element integral over $C$ lies in $D'$. This holds in each factor of a product of fields as well. Thus the normalizations computed from Artin–Schreier polynomials below are exactly those of $C$ required in the item.

Put $k=k_A$ and $l=k_B$. The perfect core $\bigcap_m l^{p^m}$ is perfect: the unique $p$th root in $l$ of an element in this intersection belongs to every $l^{p^m}$, using its $p^{m+1}$th roots. Hence $k$ is perfect. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $A$, also of $B$. If $\xi\in B$, test (A) gives $\mathfrak m_BC=\mathfrak m_C$, so the identity extension $K_1=K$ works. Otherwise fix $N>0$ with $\pi^N\xi\in B$. Apply the compatible-section node to $A/\pi^N A\to B/\pi^N B$; both maximal ideals are nilpotent and the lower residue is perfect. Lift its upper section to a set map $\sigma:l\to B$, with $\sigma(0)=0$. It preserves sums and products modulo $\pi^N B$, and $\sigma(k)\subset A+\pi^N B$. Successively subtract the residue digit and divide by $\pi$ to write $\xi=\sum_{i=1}^N\sigma(\lambda_i)\pi^{-i}+b$ with $b\in B$. Put $J=\{i:\lambda_i\notin k\}$ and $I=\{1,\ldots,N\}\setminus J$.

Keep $N$ and these sections fixed. If $j,j'=p^s j$ both belong to $J$ with $s>0$, put $h=\sum_{a=0}^{s-1}\sigma(\lambda_j^{p^a})\pi^{-jp^a}$ and replace $z$ by $z+h$. Telescoping gives $\wp(h)=-\sigma(\lambda_j)\pi^{-j}+\sigma(\lambda_j^{p^s})\pi^{-j'}$ modulo $B$. All lift errors lie in $\pi^N B$ before multiplication by a pole of order at most $j'\leq N$, so they are integral. Thus $\lambda_j$ becomes zero, $\lambda_{j'}$ becomes $\lambda_{j'}+\lambda_j^{p^s}$, and the other digits are unchanged. The number of indices outside $k$ strictly decreases: $j$ disappears and only $j'$ can change its membership. Repeating this finite descent leaves either $J=\varnothing$ or no two indices of $J$ related by multiplication by a positive power of $p$. This is the finite induction of the source, with the sign of the generator replacement corrected.

source.place: Tag 09F1, paragraph beginning Suppose that j prime, j in J; corrected telescoping sign

proof.text: If $J=\varnothing$, choose $a_i\in A$ with $\sigma(\lambda_i)-a_i\in\pi^N B$ and write $\xi=\alpha+b$, $\alpha=\sum_i a_i\pi^{-i}\in K$, $b\in B$. Reduce the pole order of $\alpha$ over $K$ as follows. If $\alpha=\pi^{-d}u$, $u\in A^\times$, and $p\mid d$, choose $a\in A$ with $\bar a^p=\bar u$ (perfectness of $k$). Replacing both $\alpha$ by $\alpha-\wp(a\pi^{-d/p})$ and $z$ by $z-a\pi^{-d/p}$ strictly lowers the pole order, since $u-a^p\in\pi A$ and $d/p<d$. The nonnegative integer pole order strictly decreases, so eventually either $\alpha\in A$ (then $\xi\in B$), or its positive pole order is prime to $p$. The unchanged integral remainder is still denoted $b$.

In the integral case of the preceding step, test (A) again gives the identity weak solution. Otherwise adjoin $w$ with $w^p-w=\alpha$ to $K$. Test (B) over $A$ makes $K_1=K[w]$ a field of degree $p$, totally ramified with $A_1$ a complete DVR; it is separable (indeed normal and separable) by the converse clause of the Artin–Schreier presentation node, since $K_1$ is the field case of $K[T]/(T^p-T-\alpha)$. The base-change node supplies the field $L_1=L\otimes_KK_1$ and its complete normalization $B_1=B\otimes_AA_1$, with $\mathfrak m_{A_1}B_1=\mathfrak m_{B_1}$. In $M\otimes_KK_1$, the variable $z-w$ satisfies $\wp(z-w)=b\in B_1$; substituting $T\mapsto T+w$ identifies this algebra with $L_1[T]/(T^p-T-b)$. This algebra is reduced (the polynomial has derivative $-1$), hence a finite product of finite field extensions of $L_1$; applying the complete-DVR normalization node to $B_1$ and each factor, the integral closure $D$ of $B_1$ is the product of the complete DVRs of the factors, so each localization $D_q$ at a maximal ideal is one of these DVRs. Test (A) over $B_1$ says $\mathfrak m_{B_1}D_q=qD_q$, i.e. each branch has ramification index one over $B_1$, and hence over $A_1$. Step 2 identifies these with the required normalizations of $C$. Their maximal ideals contract to $\mathfrak m_{A_1}$, since a uniformizer of $A_1$ generates each branch maximal ideal. This proves the weak-solution condition when $J=\varnothing$.

Now assume $J
e\varnothing$ after the finite descent. For $j\in J$, take the largest $r_j\geq0$ such that $\lambda_j\in l^{p^{r_j}}$ and write $\lambda_j=\mu_j^{p^{r_j}}$. This largest integer exists because $\lambda_j
otin igcap_m l^{p^m}=k$; thus $\mu_j
otin l^p$. The rational numbers $j p^{-r_j}$ are pairwise distinct: equality would make two indices differ by a power of $p$. Choose $r>\max_j r_j$ so large that every $d_j=j p^{r-r_j}>N$, and put $q=p^r$. Apply the approximate-root node with $h=N+1>1$ to obtain a separable totally ramified degree-$q$ extension $K_1/K$ with uniformizer $t$ of $A_1$ and $t^q=\pi+\pi^{N+1}a$. The base-change node gives a field $L_1$, complete DVR $B_1=B\otimes_AA_1$, uniformizer $t$, and residue field $l$, with $\mathfrak m_{A_1}B_1=\mathfrak m_{B_1}$.

For $1\leq i\leq N$, the identity $t^q=\pi(1+\pi^Na)$ gives $\pi^{-i}=t^{-iq}(1+\pi^Na)^i$, so $\pi^{-i}-t^{-iq}\in B_1$: its $t$-valuation is at least $q(N-i)\geq0$. For $j\in J$, section multiplicativity gives $\sigma(\lambda_j)-\sigma(\mu_j)^{p^{r_j}}\in\pi^N B$. For $i\in I$, take the unique $q$th root $\nu_i\in k$ of $\lambda_i$ and put $x_i=\sigma(\nu_i)$. Then $\sigma(\lambda_i)-x_i^q\in\pi^N B$. After multiplication by $t^{-iq}$ all these errors are still integral. Consequently, for some $b_1\in B_1$, $\xi=\sum_{i\in I}(x_i t^{-i})^q+\sum_{j\in J}(\sigma(\mu_j)t^{-d_j})^{p^{r_j}}+b_1$.

For any $v$ and integer $s\geq0$, $\wp(\sum_{a=0}^{s-1}v^{p^a})=v^{p^s}-v$, with the sum empty at $s=0$. Subtract from $z$ the sums with $(v,s)=(x_i t^{-i},r)$ for $i\in I$ and $(v,s)=(\sigma(\mu_j)t^{-d_j},r_j)$ for $j\in J$. The resulting variable $z'$ satisfies $\wp(z')=\eta=\sum_{i\in I}x_i t^{-i}+\sum_{j\in J}\sigma(\mu_j)t^{-d_j}+b_1$. Substitution in the polynomial quotient gives $M\otimes_KK_1\cong L_1[T]/(T^p-T-\eta)$. Let $j_0$ maximize $d_j$. Its maximum is unique, $d_{j_0}>N\geq i$ for $i\in I$, and $p\mid d_{j_0}$ because $r>r_{j_0}$. Thus $\eta=t^{-d_{j_0}}u$ with $u\in B_1^\times$ and residue $\bar u=\mu_{j_0}\notin l^p$.

Apply test (C) to the last equation over the complete DVR $B_1$. It says $M\otimes_KK_1$ is a field and its normalization $C_1$ is a complete DVR with $\mathfrak m_{B_1}C_1=\mathfrak m_{C_1}$. By the base-change node, $\mathfrak m_{A_1}B_1=\mathfrak m_{B_1}$, hence $\mathfrak m_{A_1}C_1=\mathfrak m_{C_1}$. Step 2 identifies $C_1$ with the integral closure of $C$ required in the item; its maximal ideal contracts to the maximal ideal of $A_1$ because $t$ generates both maximal ideals. The extension $K_1/K$ was finite separable and totally ramified by its construction. This proves every clause of the weak-solution assertion in the nonempty-$J$ case as well.
